regime.headline: Risk-on
regime.paragraph: Investors added risk across equities and credit: US Treasury yields 2Y +3bp to 4.72% and 10Y -1bp to 4.99%. The US curve saw a twist flattener in 2s10s (-4bp to 27bp). The dollar rose 0.1%, gold rose 0.5%, the S&P 500 rose 0.7% and Brent fell 1.9%. US high-yield spreads tightened 2bp. The standout move was US IG credit spread (OAS) (+2bp, 1.9x its 20-day volatility).

relationships.statement: Tighter BTP–Bund spreads signalled stronger demand for periphery risk.
relationships.lesson: BTP–Bund is the euro area's main gauge of sovereign and fragmentation risk; it usually widens with risk-off and narrows when risk appetite is strong.

relationships.statement: The Treasury curve twisted flatter: tighter policy priced while long-end yields fell on growth risk.
relationships.lesson: Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth.

relationships.statement: EUR/USD fell even as the Treasury–Bund spread narrowed.
relationships.lesson: FX tends to follow relative rates: a wider US–German yield gap raises the carry on USD versus EUR. Front-end (2Y) differentials usually matter more than 10Y.

relationships.statement: Lower oil pulled US breakevens down.
relationships.lesson: Energy feeds directly into headline inflation, so short-dated breakevens track oil closely.

relationships.statement: Gold rose despite higher real yields.
relationships.lesson: Gold pays no coupon, so higher real yields raise the opportunity cost of holding it. A break often reflects central-bank buying, geopolitical hedging or dollar moves.

interview.question: What is the market pricing for the Federal Reserve, and what changed today?
interview.answer: Policy rate 4.00%. Markets price a 20% chance of a 25bp hike at the next meeting and 2.7 hikes (67bp) over 12 months; terminal 4.93%. The 12-month pricing moved -21bp on the day. Method: Refinitiv OIS curve. Remember that one 25bp move is 25bp of pricing, so +67bp is 2.7 moves.

interview.question: Why did BTP–Bund spreads tighten?
interview.answer: BTP–Bund moved -11bp to 113bp. The spread prices Italian sovereign credit and redenomination risk relative to Germany. It widens with global risk-off, Italian fiscal or political news, or a hawkish ECB (higher rates raise debt-servicing concerns), and tightens with strong risk appetite and carry demand. The ECB's TPI backstop limits disorderly widening. Today's Euro Stoxx move was +0.8%.

interview.question: Why did the US 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The US 2Y moved +3bp and the 10Y -1bp, so 2s10s moved -4bp to 27bp: a twist flattener. Front end sold off while the long end rallied: tighter policy expected, weighing on growth. Market pricing for the Fed over 12 months moved -21bp, which is what drives the front end. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: Why did the German 10Y outperform the 2Y?
interview.answer: The German 2Y moved +5bp and the 10Y +1bp, so 2s10s moved -4bp to 28bp: a bear flattener. Front-end yields rose more than the long end: the market is pricing a more hawkish central bank. Key framework: the 2Y is anchored by expected policy over two years; the 10Y adds term premium and long-run growth and inflation expectations.

interview.question: Why did Gilts outperform Bunds?
interview.answer: 10Y Gilts moved -2bp versus +1bp for Bunds, so the spread moved -3bp to 199bp (97th percentile of the past year). Cross-market spreads remove the global rates move and isolate local drivers: domestic data surprises, relative central-bank repricing, and supply or fiscal news. Check whether the front end (2Y spread) moved too: if it did, it is a policy story; if only the long end moved, it is term premium.
